column3: The Hebrew uses two gathering verbs, first for their forces and then for assembling at Socoh; BSB combines these into one gathering statement.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses plural “camps of the Philistines”; BSB uses singular “the Philistine camp.”
The Hebrew describes the armor as a coat of “scales”; BSB uses “coat of mail.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the spear’s shaft its “wood” and its point its “flame.” It uses plural “weavers” in the beam comparison, where BSB has singular “a weaver.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB supplies Goliath. He calls himself “the Philistine,” whereas BSB has “a Philistine.”
The Hebrew twice uses a verb meaning “strike”; BSB renders both occurrences as “kill.”
The Hebrew says “Give me a man, and let us fight together”; BSB compresses this to “Give me a man to fight.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls Jesse “the man” in the final clause; BSB repeats his name.
The Hebrew repeats the verb for going in describing the older sons and explicitly introduces the names of the three sons. BSB combines this into one following statement and a list.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has no separate introductory “One day” and includes a request particle in the instruction to take the food; BSB adds the time expression and leaves the request particle implicit.
The Hebrew calls the officer “commander of the thousand”; BSB renders the number as the more general “their unit.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “battle line” in “battle line against battle line”; BSB combines this into “in formation against each other.”
The Hebrew says David left his equipment “at the hand of the keeper of the equipment”; BSB renders this as leaving supplies “in the care of the quartermaster.”
The Hebrew says he “spoke according to these words”; BSB describes him as shouting “his usual words.”
The Hebrew calls the one seen “the man”; BSB supplies Goliath.
The Hebrew says the king will make the father’s house “free in Israel”; BSB specifies that the freedom is “from taxation.”

The Hebrew’s final question uses the general noun for a word or matter; BSB specifies “a question.”
The Hebrew says he spoke the same words to another person; BSB specifies that he “asked about the offer.”
